Head unit probe
Finds out what your car actually does with the phone\'s session. Each connection runs one attempt, changing exactly one thing, and records how far it got and the exact bytes the car answered with.

How to run it
Start the engine and let the car screen finish booting.
Plug the phone into the car\'s data USB port, with a good cable.
Leave it connected for a minute. A car that refuses usually retries by itself, and each retry advances the matrix by one.
Unplug and plug back in until every attempt has been run, then share the report.

What the car presented to us
No public source records this for this model of head unit. Its issuer identifies who actually built the projection software in these cars.
What this means
This car does not require a certificate issued by Google. Nobody has published that result before — it is worth reporting.
Every identity was refused during the handshake. The alert on each row names the check that failed. This is the expected outcome, and it is the first published measurement of it.
The handshake succeeded and the car refused afterwards. It accepted the certificate as a certificate and rejected the identity, which is a more specific finding than a chain failure.
The car never spoke. That is a cable, port or connection problem rather than a verdict about certificates. Try another cable, and check the car has Android Auto enabled.

Checks
Everything checkable from the phone is in order. If nothing still happens when you plug in, the car is not offering a connection — that is a fact about the car, not about the app.
Phone supports USB accessories
The phone can be switched into accessory mode by a car.
This phone reports no USB accessory support, so a car can never hand it a connection.
Nothing in this app can work around this. Check the phone is not in a restricted or work profile.
Car connected right now
No accessory is attached.

Normal when the phone is not plugged into the car. If it *is* plugged in and this still says nothing: try another cable, use the car\'s data USB port rather than a charge-only one, and set the phone\'s USB mode to charging rather than file transfer.

Unplug and plug back in, and accept the dialog that asks whether to open this app for the accessory. Ticking \"always\" makes later connections silent.
Notifications allowed
The ongoing notification can show progress while the phone is in the car.
Denied. The probe still runs, but it has no way to show progress while the cable is in the car.
Allow notifications for this app so a running probe is visible.
Report can be saved
Results cannot be written, so nothing will survive unplugging. Check the phone has free space.
Battery restrictions
The app is exempt, so a session will not be killed mid-probe.
The app is battery-managed. Android may kill a session before the car finishes talking.
If probes keep stopping halfway, set this app\'s battery usage to unrestricted.
Has a cable ever woken the app
Never. Nothing has plugged into this phone since the app was installed.
%1$d events recorded, most recently at %2$s.

This is the important one. If it stays empty after plugging into the car, the car never switched the phone into accessory mode — so nothing the app does could have run. Suspect the cable, the port, or Android Auto not being enabled on the car, in that order.
Open app settings
What the cable did
Trying certificates
Each connection presents a different certificate and records how the car reacts. Already run once: all nine were refused with the same code.
Reading the refusal
Each connection breaks the session in a different way, to find out whether the car\'s refusal code changes. If it never changes, the code says nothing about certificates.
Projecting to the car
The next connection sends a picture to the car screen. Only worth trying once the car has been seen accepting a certificate we generated.

Codes the car gave
Different failures get different codes, so the code means something and part of it is now mapped. No public source records any of these values.
One code, and only where the session got far enough to earn a verdict. That limits what it can mean without showing it to be about certificates.
One code for every kind of failure, including ones with nothing to do with the certificate. It is a general \"something went wrong\" and tells us nothing about the trust wall.
The car has not sent a verdict in any attempt that got far enough to expect one.
